headline: Large Energy Users Pay Grid Costs
short_summary: This bill directs Dominion Energy Virginia to propose rate structures that allocate costs for increased generation capacity and distribution infrastructure to large energy users (25 MW or more), rather than residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential ratepayers, consumer advocacy groups, Governor Spanberger's administration.
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial energy users.
news_headline: Virginia energy plan targets data-center costs, rising demand.
news_summary: Virginia's 2026 Energy Plan recommends that data centers pay for the additional generation, transmission, and distribution costs they create, rather than shifting these costs to households and small businesses. This aligns with the intent of HB 1393 to ensure fairer cost allocation for major new customers.

headline: Data Centers Report Water Usage
short_summary: This bill mandates that water users providing water to data centers report total potable and reclaimed water volumes to the State Water Control Board, enhancing transparency on water consumption.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities, water conservationists, Senator Kannan Srinivasan.
opponents: Data center industry (due to reporting burden/potential scrutiny).
news_headline: As They Consider New Data Centers, States Target Water Use.
news_summary: States are increasingly focusing on data center water use, with Virginia's SB 553 requiring water suppliers to identify potable and reclaimed water volumes delivered to data centers. This legislation aims to provide clarity on projected and actual water demand.

headline: Localities Assess Data Center Siting, Noise
short_summary: This bill requires site assessments for new high-energy use facilities, including sound profile studies near residential areas and schools, and allows localities to consider impacts on water, agriculture, and historic sites.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near potential data center sites, environmental groups, Delegate Joshua Thomas, Delegate Sam Rasoul.
opponents: Data center developers, real estate industry (due to increased regulatory burden and potential restrictions).
news_headline: A Roanoke Delegate Helped Write Virginia's New Data Center Law.
news_summary: Virginia's new law, HB 153, requires developers of large data centers to conduct site assessments, including noise studies for homes and schools within 500 feet. While it mandates studies, it does not set specific noise limits or water caps, leaving some discretion to local authorities.
